- When sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -1.00) and model overreacts with a spike, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., +1.00 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overestimate; cap forecast at +5% above recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment is flat or mildly negative (0.33–0.67) and model forecasts persistently above true price, apply downward bias of 2–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- When news volume is low (0.0) and sentiment is volatile, model often overfits recent spikes; smooth forecast by averaging last 5 days’ true values.  
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, apply “lag correction”: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.  
- For sentiment change > +1.00 or -1.00, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment change as a 3-day moving average to adjust forecast slope.
